name: MAX31850K 1-Wire thermocouple amplifier
description: Maxim/Analog Devices cold-junction-compensated K-type thermocouple-to-digital converter on a 1-Wire bus (family code 3Bh): thermocouple range -270 to +1372 °C in 0.25 °C steps (14-bit), cold-junction temperature in 0.0625 °C steps, open/short-circuit fault flags, AD0-AD3 location pins. Chip runs on 3.0-3.7 V; the board regulates VIN 3.3-5 V down to 3.3 V, and DATA is 3.3 V logic only. Sold as: Adafruit 1-Wire Thermocouple Amplifier MAX31850K breakout (product 1727), 8-pin header GND, VIN, 3V3, A0, A1, A2, A3, DATA plus a 2-way screw terminal (YELLOW+, RED-) for the thermocouple; no pull-up on DATA (add 4.7 kΩ to 3.3 V).
eli5: Plug a thermocouple wire into it and it tells your board how hot the tip is, even inside an oven or a flame, over a single data wire.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply in, 3.3-5 V, to the on-board 3.3 V regulator

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: 3.3 V output of the on-board regulator (up to 100 mA); not a supply input, leave unconnected

pins.name: A0
pins.description: Location address bit AD0 (read back in scratchpad byte 4); tied to GND by a solder jumper, leave unconnected

pins.name: A1
pins.description: Location address bit AD1; tied to GND by a solder jumper, leave unconnected

pins.name: A2
pins.description: Location address bit AD2; tied to GND by a solder jumper, leave unconnected

pins.name: A3
pins.description: Location address bit AD3; tied to GND by a solder jumper, leave unconnected

pins.name: DATA
pins.description: 1-Wire data (DQ), open-drain, 3.3 V logic only; needs a 4.7 kΩ pull-up to 3.3 V (not on the board)

buildNotes: K-type thermocouples only. Yellow (+, chromel) lead to YELLOW+, red (-, alumel) lead to RED- on the screw terminal; thermocouple wire cannot be soldered.
Fit a 4.7 kΩ pull-up from DATA to 3.3 V; the board has none. DATA must never see 5 V.
Send Convert T (44h), wait at least 100 ms (tCONV max), then Read Scratchpad (BEh) and check the CRC (MicroPython's ds18x20 module does the commands and CRC).
Thermocouple temperature = bits 15..2 of bytes 0-1 as a signed 14-bit number x 0.25 °C. Bit 0 of byte 0 set = fault; bits 0/1/2 of byte 2 say open circuit / short to GND / short to VDD.
MicroPython's ds18x20.scan() skips family 3Bh: find the chips with onewire.OneWire.scan() and keep ROMs starting with 0x3B.
Do not ground either thermocouple lead or let the probe touch grounded metal: that is reported as a short-circuit fault.
Power it from VIN; parasite power from DATA would need a strong pull-up during each conversion.

example.code:
import machine, onewire, time
from max31850 import MAX31850

tc = MAX31850(onewire.OneWire(machine.Pin({DATA})))
roms = tc.scan()
print('found', len(roms))
while True:
    tc.convert()  # Convert T, waits 100 ms
    for rom in roms:
        print('TC=%.2fC' % tc.read_temp(rom))
    time.sleep(1)
